items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: It was "Dissonance in Blues," an original that Gerald wrote especially to feature me on the bass.

ctx.x: In Imperial, yes. And two months later Universal (I think that was the name of the label) came out with "Night Train," and the rest of that is history. Every time I see him I say, "See, you should listen to somebody that knows." He missed a windfall by passing that one up.
You were telling me also that you recorded a bass solo with Gerald Wilson that is credited on the record to somebody else. Do you want to tell me that story?

Yeah. It was "Dissonance in Blues," an original that Gerald wrote especially to feature me on the bass. I saw it lately. Some bootleggers in Europe or somewhere had copied the record, and they didn't know who the bass player was, so they just inserted some name. But for posterity and everything, that's me playing the bass solo on "Dissonance And Blues." That was my first solo attempt on a record.

items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I walked around with Red Callender and Buddy Collette, you know.

ctx.x: Oh, Raiders of the Lost Arc?

Yeah, yeah, and we do all of that, doing it in harmony, you know what I mean? Broken up, man, and I enjoyed being in that. And now I can say, John is the president of it now, so many things have changed. Like the Local 47, I made the motion, see now, there were other guys doing things, we were all doing things walking around getting white musicians to sign a petition to do, you know, to have no suffering locals, you know what I mean. So I being from Detroit, as I said, Detroit they’re locals already, you know,…

back after the road with Count and I say, “Well, how things going now with the amalgamation?” He said, “Well, you know, nothing is really happening now Gerald, it’s kind of in limbo now, you know.” So I said, “Okay.” So I knew a lawyer from Detroit that I met when I was going to school, he had moved to California, his name is Calvin Porter, Calvin Porter.
